headline: Approved new siding at 173 Woodland Street and solar panels at 35 Broadview Street; continued 141 Woodland Street driveway request to November 18, 2026.
summary: Most hearings covered repairs and changes to homes in the historic district. Siding was being replaced after a July 4, 2026 hailstorm, and the driveway request was continued so the homeowner could provide more information.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 23, 2026 regular meeting, as amended, 5-0.

Approved installation of twelve rooftop solar panels at 35 Broadview Street, 5-0.
Continued the driveway application for 141 Woodland Street to November 18, 2026, 5-0.

Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
BRISTOL HISTORIC DISTRICT COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF WEDNESDAY OCTOBER 28, 2026 
 
 
By: Chairman Collins Time: 5:00 P.M. Place: City Hall 
    111 North Main Street 
    Council Chambers 
    First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS: NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: Andrew E. Collins, Chair X  
 Karen Stevens, Vice-Chair X  
 Colleen Nicastro X  
 Alicia M. Jennings X  
 Paden Dickinson X  
    
ALTERNATE MEMBERS: Gregory Hartmann  X  
 Jason Michael Messier X  
 Jodi Maro X  
    
STAFF: Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
    
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Chairman Collins, the meeting was called to order at 5:00 P.M.  
 
Chairman Collins reminded the Commission the next regular meeting is Wednesday, November 18, 2026. 
 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
3. Public Participation 
There was no Public Participation. 
 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting — September 23, 2026 
 
Chairman Collins noted two corrections to the September 23, 2026 regular meeting minutes as follows: 
1. “Call to Order” should read “Called to Order” 
2. Commissioner Maro was recused from one of the application votes, but it wasn’t noted in the Minutes. 
 
Motion: Move to approve the minutes of the September 23, 2026, regular meeting, as amended. 
 
By: Commissioner Nicastro Seconded: Vice-Chair Stevens
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
All were in favor and the Minutes were accepted into the record as amended.  
 
At this time the Chair called for a motion to move item 6. Old Business a. Application Recusal – Update up for 
discussion. Attorney Wyland Dale Clift was present from the Corporation Council’s office to speak to this item.  
 
Vice-Chair Stevens made the motion to move the item forward. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Nicastro.  
All were in favor and the motion was accepted into the record. 
 
Attorney Clift heard from the Commissioners and the City Planner regarding their recusal practice having been when  
a commissioner was within 500 feet of the property represented in any given application. The practice had led to  
several recusals at the September 2026 meeting. The question was whether the practice was necessary and/or if it  
could be adjusted to allow the hearing process to remain efficient and fair to both residents and the Commissioners.  
 
Discussion followed with the City Planner providing background of when he’d first brought his concern about proper  
recusals being done and that 500 feet was the guideline. Then, given the instances of recusals at the last  
Commission Meeting, he spoke again with Corporation Council again, and they agreed on a distance of 100 feet, as  
well as the standard basis of conflict of interest. Discussion followed. 
 
Attorney Clift noted a land use statute regarding states that a commissioner should recuse themselves when an 
application when they are directly or indirectly interested in a personal or financial sense of the approval of the 
application. He also provided additional guidance for Commissioners to disclose to applicants if they live within  
the 100 feet and provide the applicant with the opportunity to request the Commissioner not sit to hear the  
application. The Chair noted that the main goal is to avoid the appearance of a potential conflict of intertest.  
 
5. Public Hearings 
 
a. Application #2026-10-01 — Request for a Certificate of Appropriateness for the installation of new siding, 
gutters, soffit and all related siding accessories at 173 Woodland Street; Assessor's Map 25, Lot 60/14; Crystal 
Pelletier owner/applicant. 
 
Chairman Collins designated regular Commissioners Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins to vote on 
Application # 2026-10-01. Alternate Member Hartmann recused himself as his home is adjacent to the property in 
the application. 
 
Crystal Pelletier, 173 Woodland Street: The contractor, Taylor Tobias of BNF Construction, was on the call along with  
the homeowner, Ms. Pelletier. The project was the result of the July 4, 2026 hailstorm with 100 hail strikes on the  
home, and hail ranging from ½ inch to 2 inches in size. The current siding is no longer made, and spot or patch  
repair is not good for the situation. The applicant noted that the insurance company was part of the assessment  
process. 
 
The proposed new siding would be white and has a slight woodgrain detail. The windows are staying, and there will  
be new wraps around them as well as new aluminum. The project includes nearly identical/ like for like gutter  
replacements. It was confirmed that neither the homes columns nor railing sustained hail damage.  
 
The new siding is Double 5 which indicates the width of it. It is the closest available option to what is currently on  
the home. It was confirmed that no original, historic photos of the home are available
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
There was no further discussion or additional questions from the Commissioners. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Commissioner Nicastro Seconded: Vice-Chair Stevens 
 
For: Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins. 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
The Chair noted that the July 4, 2026 hailstorm caused a lot of damage in the Historic District neighborhood. He also  
noted that the Commission can’t legislate the exterior color of the homes in the district, and the Commission  
appreciated knowing the plans for the various pieces of the project. There were no concerns noted among the  
Commissioners. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #2026-10-01 — Request for a Certificate of Appropriateness for the 
installation of new siding, gutters, soffit and all related siding accessories at 173 Woodland Street; 
Assessor's Map 25, Lot 60/14; Crystal Pelletier owner/applicant, in accordance with the plot plan and 
information submitted, be APPROVED because of the following reasons: 
 
This Approval is subject to the following conditions: 
1) Prior to a final Certificate of Occupancy being issued, the Land Use Staff will conduct an inspection to certify 
compliance with the terms and conditions of the approval. 
2) Any deviation from the approved plans may require approval of the Commission after staff review and 
discussion with the Vice Chairman. 
3) Any transfer or assignment of this permit shall require approval of the Commission. 
4) This permit may be revoked if the permittee exceeds the conditions or limitations of this permit or has 
secured the permit through deception or inaccurate information. 
 
By: Commissioner Jennings Seconded: Vice-Chair Stevens 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
The application is approved. 
Alternate Member Hartmann returned to the meeting at this time. 
 
b. Application #2026-10-02 — Request for a Certificate of Appropriateness for the installation of twelve (12) 
rooftop solar panels at 35 Broadview Street; Assessor's Map 25A, Lot 77; Kelly Carson for Sunrun, applicant; 
Luis Martinez, owner. 
 
Chairman Collins designated regular Commissioners Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens and Collins to vote on 
Application # 2026-10-02.  Kelly Carson-of Sunrun, 712 Brook Street, Rocky Hill, representing the property owner, 
Luis Martinez, 35 Broadview Street were on Zoom. 
 
Ms. Carson spoke regarding the installation of the panels referencing and the shared images showing the proposed  
panel layout and placement of various related items such as the battery.
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
She confirmed the panels would be installed in one day, and if the project is approved, they would move forward  
with the next steps under the guidance of the City Planner. Ms. Carson advised that Sunrun doesn’t begin work  
without permit approval. 
 
It was confirmed that all the panels would be placed on the front facing portion of the roof because that is where the  
best sun exposure is. Ms. Carson confirmed that while panels could be placed on the back facing portion of the roof,  
there is less sun exposure there, so they’d need to place more panels to achieve a similar benefit to the homeowner.  
 
Vice-Chair Stevens asked about the age of the roof stating the question is to protect or make the homeowner aware  
of the process and expense if a roof replacement is needed after the panels have been installed. Ms. Carson noted  
that it is their company’s policy to remove and reinstall the panels if a new roof is needed after the fact. 
 
There was no further discussion or additional questions from the Commissioners. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Commissioner Nicastro Seconded: Commissioner Dickinson 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
The Chair noted that this was a standard solar panel application for the Commission and that their jurisdiction is  
limited by the State guidelines. These guidelines speak to the Commission’s oversight if panels will diminish the  
Historic District if installed. There was no additional discussion. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #2026-10-02 — Request for a Certificate of Appropriateness for the 
installation of twelve (12) rooftop solar panels at 35 Broadview Street; Assessor's Map 25A, Lot 77; 
Kelly Carson for Sunrun, applicant; Luis Martinez, owner, in accordance with the plot plan and 
information submitted, be APPROVED because of the following reasons: 
 
This Approval is subject to the following conditions: 
1) Prior to a final Certificate of Occupancy being issued, the Land Use Staff will conduct an inspection to certify 
compliance with the terms and conditions of the approval. 
2) Any deviation from the approved plans may require approval of the Commission after staff review and 
discussion with the Vice Chairman. 
3) Any transfer or assignment of this permit shall require approval of the Commission. 
4) This permit may be revoked if the permittee exceeds the conditions or limitations of this permit or has 
secured the permit through deception or inaccurate information. 
 
By: Vice-Chair Stevens Seconded: Commissioner Jennings 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
The application is approved.
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
c. Application #2026-10-03 — Request for a Certificate of Appropriateness for the: 1. paving/expansion of an 
existing driveway (1 vehicle to 2 vehicles) on Woodland Street; 2. paving/installation of a new driveway (2 
vehicles) on Oakland Street; at 141 Woodland Street; Assessor's Map 25, Lot 52; Sabrena Lawrence, 
owner/applicant. 
 
Chairman Collins designated regular Commissioners Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens and Collins to vote on 
Application #2026-10-03. Alternate Member Moro recused herself due to her living in the close proximity to the 
property. 
 
Sabrena Lawrence, 141 Woodland Street: Ms. Lawrence moved to 141 Woodland Street with her family in June 2022.  
At the time, the driveway was sufficient for their use. They now have additional drivers with their children having  
grown, and with no off-street parking allowed, they looked into expanding the existing driveway and adding a second  
driveway to the property. Ms. Lawrence stated she had spoken with Sean Harris from the City’s Public Works  
Department street division to confirm they could expand and build as noted. It was her understanding that they  
could proceed with the project and that she received contractor leads from Mr. Harris. Note: Both driveway projects  
have been completed at the time of this hearing. 
 
The City Planner noted that no driveway permits have been issued by Public Works, and there would need to be two  
permits, one for the expansion on Woodland and one for the addition of a new driveway on Oakland. He also noted  
that the driveway needs to be 50 feet from the intersection, but he measured it and it is closer to 45 feet. It was also  
noted that curbing was cut, and it is unlikely that the City would have approved that.  
 
Commissioners questioned why asphalt was used instead of concrete which the original driveway was made of. Ms.  
Lawrence believed the asphalt would provide a cleaner look and use. She also believed that the work had been done 
properly regarding permits based on conversation she had with the contractor.  
 
The Chair expressed concern regarding insufficient information provided with the application, and said there should 
be much more detail provided, including materials listed. The Commission was in agreement that the new driveways 
were a substantial change from the original, and the Vice-Chair noted the Commission had previously denied other 
driveway applications on this street (Oakland Street).  
 
There was no additional discussion. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Vice-Chair Stevens Seconded: Commissioner Jennings 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
  
The Chair stated he was unable to approve the application as presented citing the lack of substance and that a lot  
more information was needed, including the survey information the City Planner mentioned, and copies of the  
driveway permits that were approved. He also spoke with the Building Department regarding what is needed. The 
Vice-Chair said that while she understood the property’s limitations, she wouldn’t necessarily approve permanent 
driveway expansions.
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 6 – 
 
After discussions, the Commission chose to continue the application to provide the homeowner with an opportunity 
to return with the additional information they requested. A motion to reopen the hearing for Application #2026-10-03 
was made by Vice-Chair Stevens and was seconded by Commissioner Nicastro. All were in favor and the hearing was 
reopened. 
 
Vice-Chair Stevens then made the following motion: 
 
MOTION: Move to continue Application #2026-10-03 to be heard at the November 18, 2026 Historic District 
Meeting. 
 
By: Vice-Chair Stevens Seconded: Commissioner Jennings 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins 
Against: None 
Abstained: None 
 
The application is continued to the November 18, 2026. 
 
Alternate Commissioner Maro returned to the meeting at this time. 
 
8.  Staff Reports 
 
a. 14 Bradley Street — Roofing 
b. 62 Bradley St. — Roofing 
c. 18 Broadview Street — Roofing 
d. 197 Grove Street – Roofing 
e. 207 Grove Street – Roofing 
 
The City Planner advised the Commission on the above noted roofing projects which received Administrative 
Approval. He confirmed that all were related to hailstorm damage. For the record, 14 Bradley Street is the home of 
Alternate Member Hartmann and the repairs are not visible from the road. 
 
f. 132 Stearns Street – Project Update 
 
The City Planner reported that he’d received an email from the homeowner stating they’d had difficulty finding a 
contractor to do the work, but they have one now. Photos were shared showing the work in progress and the 
improved appearance. 
 
g. 134 Woodland Street – Awning Replacement 
          The City Planner shared the awnings that will be replaced in kind.  
          The existing awnings have been in place since 1981 (photos were provided to the Commission). 
 
h. Preservation Connecticut Workshop 
      The Commission received the following items in their electronic packets: A flyer dated September 22, 2026,  
      regarding a Statewide Local Historic District Workshop, jointly hosted by CT SHPO and Preservation CT 
         Resources from the Cheshire meeting attended by the Chair were emailed to the Commissioners for review. 
 
i.     Yearly Summary of Commission Actions Report 
 The City Planner reported that the Yearly Summaries were last filed in 2021.   
 He will be writing the reports from 2021 through 2025 with 2026 to follow.
Bristol Historic District Commission  Regular Meeting of October 28, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 7 – 
 
j. Commissioner Appointments – Dickinson 
Commissioner Dickinson introduced himself to the Commission. 
 
9.  Adjournment 
 
Chairman Collins designated regular Commissioners Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens Dickinson and Collins to vote on the 
adjournment. 
 
MOTION: Move to adjourn at 6:10 P.M. 
 
By: Vice-Chair Stevens Seconded: Commissioner Nicastro 
 
For:  Dickinson, Jennings, Nicastro, Stevens, Collins. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 6:10 P.M. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary 
 
 
 
 
Andrew E. Collins, Chair
